title: Ines and the Trail
premise: Mirabel Montrose, a riverboat captain hiding from a past he refuses to name, agrees to ferry dying prospector Elias Ines and his estranged daughter upriver to a lost mining claim before monsoon season seals the gorge. Along the way, Mirabel discovers the map leads not to gold but to evidence that could exonerate—or condemn—the man who raised him, forcing him to choose between loyalty to his crew's found family and the truth he has buried for twelve years. When rival claim-jumpers and the rising river close in, Mirabel must reveal who he really is to save them all. The expedition reaches the claim as the monsoon breaks; Mirabel gives the truth to Ines's daughter, keeps only the family he found aboard, and runs the flooded gorge home with nothing left to hide.
about_author: Vesper Hartwell is the pen name of a former deckhand turned novelist who spent six seasons working freight rivers in Southeast Asia before writing full-time. Their fiction blends nautical realism with quiet character studies of people who live at the edge of maps.

chapters.title: The Sandbar's Mood
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He reads the river at dawn, dodges a debt collector in port, and establishes his rule: no names, no pasts, no passengers. Emotional beat: comfortable isolation about to crack.

chapters.title: A Man Made of Dust
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A coughing stranger, Elias Ines, offers an impossible fare: passage up the Serein Gorge before monsoon. Mirabel refuses. Beat: curiosity he doesn't want.

chapters.title: The Map on Oiled Silk
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Dying, he shows Mirabel the map and asks not for gold but for delivery—and silence. Mirabel still refuses. Beat: temptation wearing the mask of charity.

chapters.title: Ines
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Elias's daughter arrives searching for her father, carrying twelve years of resentment and a photograph. She books passage on Mirabel's boat under a false name. Beat: two liars recognize each other.

chapters.title: Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Introduce the crew: engineer Odile, deckhand Pao, cook Bram—each one running from something. They vote to take the job over Mirabel's objection. Beat: found family asserting itself.

chapters.title: Cast Off
chapters.summary: Pao's POV. Departure at first light; the boat takes on cargo crates Elias insists stay sealed. Ines watches her father too closely. Beat: unease beneath adventure's thrill.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Miles
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Flashback fragments: the trial he fled, the man who raised him, why he measures life in miles. Beat: grief disguised as routine.

chapters.title: First Rapids
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A technical run through the Widow's Teeth rapids bonds crew and passengers; Ines proves unexpectedly capable. Beat: earned respect.

chapters.title: The Sealed Crates
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Curiosity wins; Bram peeks and finds survey instruments and ore samples—not treasure hunting gear but evidence-gathering gear. Beat: suspicion planted.

chapters.title: What Papa Buried
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She confronts Elias; he admits the claim is real but won't say what he actually found there. Beat: loyalty vs. truth, first collision.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Water
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Another boat shadows them—a claim-jumping outfit called the Corvus Line, captained by a man who looks familiar. Beat: the past closing in.

chapters.title: Port of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Pao's POV. Resupply stop; Pao learns the Corvus Line has been asking about a map by description. Someone talked. Beat: paranoia spreads.

chapters.title: The Captain Who Looked Back
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He recognizes the Corvus captain: Renn Voss, the investigator who once hunted his guardian's case. Mirabel nearly turns back. Beat: fear vs. duty.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warnings
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Radio reports put the storm ten days out; the gorge will flood and trap them. The schedule becomes a countdown. Beat: ticking clock engaged.

chapters.title: Ines Learns to Read Water
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Mirabel teaches her the river; she teaches him that hiding isn't the same as peace. Quiet chapter. Beat: intimacy without confession.

chapters.title: The Corvus Offers Terms
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Voss hails them mid-river: hand over the map and Elias, walk away rich. Mirabel refuses—and realizes Voss knows his old name. Beat: stakes made personal.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The fuel line is cut overnight; they lose a day repairing it while the Corvus gains ground. Trust frays. Beat: the enemy inside the walls.

chapters.title: Elias Confesses—Partly
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He tells Ines the claim holds records proving a mine disaster was covered up—records naming names. He omits one name. Beat: half-truths as betrayal.

chapters.title: Night Portage
chapters.summary: Pao's POV. The crew hauls the boat around a collapsed channel by lantern light, near-mutiny turning into fierce solidarity. Beat: found family forged in labor.

chapters.title: The Name on the Records
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel glimpses the manifest through Elias's delirium and sees his guardian's name among the guilty. His whole identity tilts. Beat: devastating midpoint revelation.

chapters.title: Run the Devil's Throat
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. To make up lost time they run an unrunnable rapid; the boat cracks a seam and barely survives. Beat: terror converting doubt into commitment.

chapters.title: What Mirabel Buried
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She finds Mirabel burning a letter from his old life; he finally admits who he is and why he fled. Beat: truth traded for trust.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. If the records are true, the man who saved him helped kill eleven miners. Mirabel wants to sink the evidence. Ines begs him not to. Beat: theme stated in flesh.

chapters.title: The Corvus Boards
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Voss catches them at a bend; a tense standoff ends when Elias collapses and Voss—unexpectedly—lets them go, saying he wants the truth published, not buried. Ambiguous ally? Beat: moral complication.

chapters.title: Fever Dreams
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Delirious, Elias confesses everything to Ines: the disaster, the cover-up, and that Mirabel's guardian took the fall for men still powerful. Beat: pity dissolving resentment.

chapters.title: Ines Decides
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She chooses truth over her father's reputation, aligning with Mirabel against her own blood. Beat: loyalty redefined.

chapters.title: The Storm Arrives Early
chapters.summary: Pao's POV. Monsoon hits the headwaters; the river begins rising days ahead of forecast. Two days of margin become hours. Beat: dread.

chapters.title: The Claim
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. They reach the site: a drowned adit, a strongbox of ledgers and photographs. Elias, barely conscious, asks Mirabel to read them aloud. Beat: solemn discovery.

chapters.title: Reading the Dead
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The ledgers confirm everything—including a final page Elias hid: proof Mirabel's guardian was the one whistleblower, murdered for it. Beat: grief and vindication entwined.

chapters.title: Voss Returns
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The Corvus arrives—but Voss comes unarmed, offering his boat's radio and his testimony if they publish together. Mirabel must decide whether to trust a hunter. Beat: grace from an unexpected quarter.

chapters.title: The Rising
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The gorge floods behind them; escape means running forty miles of whitewater in a storm, at night, overloaded. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Elias's Last Mile
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias dies as they cast off, asking Ines to tell it all and Mirabel to stop measuring life in miles. Beat: sorrow as fuel.

chapters.title: The Gorge in Flood
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The climactic run: strainers, whirlpools, a near-capsize where Pao goes overboard and Ines pulls him out using everything Mirabel taught her. Beat: every skill and bond tested.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. They lose the cargo, nearly lose the boat, and save each other. The ledgers survive because Ines strapped them to her own chest. Beat: values proven by sacrifice.

chapters.title: Daylight
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. They clear the gorge into calm water as the storm spends itself. Silence, then laughter, then weeping. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At the delta town, they give the ledgers to a journalist and Voss signs his affidavit. Mirabel uses his real name for the first time in twelve years. Beat: liberation through exposure.

chapters.title: Settlements
chapters.summary: Pao's POV. Aftermath vignettes: the mine's victims compensated, the guilty named, debts paid or forgiven. Beat: justice without triumphalism.

chapters.title: Refit
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The crew repairs the boat together, arguing and laughing; Ines is offered a place aboard and takes it. Beat: found family formalized.

chapters.title: Miles and Years
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Final solo scene: Mirabel scatters Elias's ashes at the Widow's Teeth, then steers downstream toward a future measured in both miles and years. Beat: peace earned.

chapters.title: The Trail Continues
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, brief rotating passages. One year later: the boat runs a new route with new passengers, Ines at the wheel, Mirabel teaching the next stray how to read the sandbar's mood. Beat: the story becomes a tradition.
